about: What each SDK's speed and load runner measures. A measure with 'since' is run only by the SDKs it names, from the version given for each. Unless a measure's 'about' says otherwise, a runner installs Baton through its MCP install path with default settings and an HTTP sink with default settings, sending to collector/fake_collector.py, started with --no-events, in the measure's 'collector' mode ('down': a port nobody listens on). The server has a tool 'echo', which returns its 'text' argument, and a tool 'large', which takes no arguments and returns a text of the measure's 'result_bytes' bytes: 'hello ' repeated and cut to that length. A client in the same process, over the SDK's in-process transport, calls echo with text 'hello' and nothing else, except in 'large_result', where it calls large. Each measure starts its own collector. Each server it runs gets a new client, and an install unless it is the server without Baton. Each install handle is closed after its server's calls, and the measure ends by stopping the collector. 'concurrency' is how many calls are in flight at once on each client; 'warmup' calls run first and are not timed. Times are wall-clock per call, from the client's call to its answer. The runner writes one JSON file per run, shaped as 'result' says. scripts/compare_bench.py reads a set of these files and prints a table.
bar: The numbers compare two versions of one SDK on one machine. They are not what a vendor sees in production: the collector is local and the client is in the same process. The exception is a measure's 'limits': over 'repeats' runs of that measure alone, each named metric's median must be under its limit. scripts/check_bench_limit.py runs and checks them. A measure's 'noise_floor' gives, per metric and SDK, the change between runs of one version that is still noise.

measures.name: overhead
measures.about: The time Baton adds to a call. The same calls run first on a server without Baton, then on one with it. 'added_*' is the Baton figure less the plain one.

measures.name: burst
measures.about: 10,000 calls as fast as the client can make them. The same calls run first on a server without Baton: 'plain_*' are its figures, and 'added_*' the Baton figure less the plain one. A full garbage collection runs before each of the two. 'emitted' is 2 per call, its tool_call_start and tool_call_end, warmup calls included. 'delivered' is how many of those the collector accepted once close returned; 'lost' is the rest.

measures.name: outage_hang
measures.about: As 'burst', with the collector taking every request and never answering. Calls must not slow down, and close must keep its budget.

measures.name: outage_down
measures.about: As 'burst', with nothing listening at the collector's address, so every connection is refused.

measures.name: memory
measures.about: Whether memory grows with calls. The live heap, after a full garbage collection, is read after the warmup, after half the calls and after all of them. 'growth_per_call_bytes' is the growth over the second half, divided by its calls: near 0 when nothing leaks. The live heap is Python's tracemalloc total, Node's heapUsed (run with --expose-gc), or Go's HeapAlloc.

measures.name: memory_outage
measures.about: As 'memory', with the collector taking every request and never answering, so the sink's buffer stays full and every send waits for its timeout.

measures.name: large_result
measures.about: As 'overhead', with every call returning about 50 KB, which Baton captures whole by default. 'emitted', 'delivered' and 'lost' are as in 'burst', for the Baton server. 'heap_growth_bytes' is the Baton server's live heap, read as in 'memory', after the calls and before close, less that after the warmup. It holds the events still queued, and leftovers of earlier measures freed during the calls count against it.

measures.name: serve_overhead
measures.about: As 'overhead', for a vendor whose own code answers MCP and passes each message through the SDK's serve. The vendor's dispatch function answers a tools/call of echo with its 'text' argument. The collector also serves this measure's 'settings' from GET /v0/settings. The same message, a tools/call of echo with arguments 'text' 'hello' and 'user_goal' '1: say hello', goes first to the dispatch alone, then through serve on a client made with the DSN http://k@127.0.0.1:<port>/ten_0123abcd/v, Console settings, the tool list [echo] given up front, and its default sink. The caller is principal 'u1' of organization 'o1' with label 'starter', so it is matched against 'enterprise' first and lands in 'everyone'. The plain calls run before the client is made. The runner then sends a tools/list through serve as that caller until echo's schema no longer requires user_goal ('everyone' makes it optional), and only then warms up and times. Calls run one at a time. Python times its blocking Client.

result.version: the version of the SDK measured, as its package says
result.source: 'published' for a version from the package registry, 'checkout' for the code in the repository
result.runtime: the language runtime and its version
result.cpu: the CPU model as the OS names it (on Linux, the first 'model name' in /proc/cpuinfo), else 'unknown'; shared CI machines differ in speed. Optional: kept results may lack it
result.max_rss_bytes: the process's peak resident memory once the measures before 'memory' have run, since Python's heap reading itself takes memory; at exit when no memory measure ran
result.measures: an object with a member per measure run, each an object with a number per metric. A run of one measure alone has that member only, and a version before a measure's 'since' leaves it out
